thread:
jun: Quick check — we're bringing up Aquila-7B-Lite for eval on staging. LICENSE.txt in the release zip has some odd clauses. TL;DR from license: commercial use allowed with attribution, but 'redistribution of model weights is prohibited'. Can someone confirm how that applies to quantization and hosting?

tara_legal: Short answer: probably fine to host as a service, but distributing weights (even quantized) looks disallowed without explicit permission. Paste of the relevant lines from LICENSE.txt we saw:

```
Redistribution: The model weights in whole or part may not be redistributed, resold, or sublicensed.
Derivatives: Transformations of the model (including quantization or pruning) are permitted for internal use only. Distribution of transformed weights requires explicit written permission from Aquila-Labs.
Attribution: Any public use of the model must credit "Aquila-Labs (2025)" in visible product documentation.
```

tara_legal: So: hosting via our Hosted API = allowed (it's running, not handing over weights). Shipping a Docker with the quantized bin to a customer = distribution, so not allowed per that snippet.

sam: Also flag — the attribution clause requires visible credit. Does that mean in-app footer or docs is enough? Has anyone seen precedent?

maria: For Dedicated (we run for a customer on reserved infra) they access via our API endpoints, we don't hand over weights. Should be covered under 'hosting'. But Private/on-prem packages where the customer runs model on-prem is likely a redistribution event.

oliver: Implementation note: our quantize pipeline emits `model.q4_*` files. We currently have a weights-export gating PR but need to be explicit: any export that leaves our infra must be blocked unless legal clears. @tara_legal can we get a quick rule added to model-onboarding checklist?

tara_legal: Yep — proposed steps: 1) Do not export/distribute quantized weights off our infra without explicit upstream permission. 2) Hosting via API (hosted or dedicated) is allowed but ensure attribution placed where product-visible. 3) For Private/on-prem, either get upstream redistribution permission or require customer to obtain license directly. I'll add this to the onboarding checklist.

jun: For evals: we plan to run quantized benchmarks internally and publish aggregate metrics and sample outputs. Is publishing prompt+output pairs okay?

tara_legal: Generally publishing generated outputs is fine unless the license says otherwise. Add attribution and scrub PII. If publishing verbatim model outputs with research paper, include the attribution line and a short note on evaluation setup.

sam: One more nuance — some licenses treat 'derivative' differently. Quantized weights might be considered a derivative, but if the license forbids redistribution of "model weights in whole or part" that covers quantized too. We should treat any weights file as covered.

maria: Action items for infra/eng:
- enforce export gating on `model.q*` artifacts (internal s3 + ACLs)
- add checklist item to `model-onboarding` about redistribution permissions
- add required in-product attribution text to `attribution-templates` repo

oliver: I'll open a tiny PR to block `s3://artifacts/weights/*` from public export and add a pre-merge checklist entry.

tara_legal: I'll reach out to Aquila-Labs legal to request written permission for two things: (A) redistribution of quantized weights to enterprise customers under our reseller agreement, (B) a canonical attribution string we can use in UI. ETA 2-3 business days. :white_check_mark: 

jun: Thanks — tagging this thread on the onboarding ticket so we don't forget. If they deny redistribution we'll need an alternate plan for on-prem (customer obtains license or we provide a hosted-only solution).

oliver: noted. will proceed with gating and internal bench only.

sam: thx all :thumbsup:
